{{Distinguish|Rayleigh scattering}}

In [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]] a '''Rayleigh mixture distribution''' is a weighted mixture of multiple [[probability distribution]]s where the weightings are equal to the weightings of a [[Rayleigh distribution]].<ref name="karim2011">Karim R., Hossain P., Begum S., and Hossain F., "Rayleigh Mixture Distribution", Journal of Applied Mathematics, Vol. 2011, {{doi|10.1155/2011/238290|doi-access=free}} (2011).</ref> Since the [[probability density function]] for a (standard) Rayleigh distribution is given by<ref name="jackson1954">Jackson J.L., "Properties of the Rayleigh Distribution", Johns Hopkins University (1954).</ref>

:<math>f(x;\sigma) = \frac{x}{\sigma^2} e^{-x^2/2\sigma^2}, \quad x \geq 0,</math>

Rayleigh mixture distributions have probability density functions of the form

:<math>f(x;\sigma,n) = \int_0^{\infty} \frac{re^{-r^2/2\sigma^2}}{\sigma^2} \tau(x,r;n) \,\mathrm{d}r,</math>

where <math>\tau(x,r;n)</math> is a well-defined probability density function or [[sampling distribution]].<ref name="karim2011" />

The Rayleigh mixture distribution is one of many types of [[compound distribution]]s in which the appearance of a value in a sample or population might be interpreted as a function of other underlying random variables. Mixture distributions are often used in [[mixture models]], which are used to express probabilities of sub-populations within a larger population.
